Rashi on Bava Metzia 63b:10:1.hebrew: אגר נטר ליה - שכר המתנה. אי מוזיל גבי משום המתנה, שמקדים לו המעות והמקח אין לו למוכר עכשיו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 63b:10:1.english: Payment for his waiting - Payment for waiting. If he lowers [the price] for him because of the waiting, in that [the buyer] advances the money to him while the seller does not have the merchandise now.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 63b:10:2.english: To a wax seller - A seller of wax.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 63b:10:3.hebrew: ד' ד' - חלות שעוה בזוזא:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 63b:10:3.english: Four, four - [Four] loaves of wax for a zuz.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 63b:10:4.hebrew: יהיבנא לך ה' ה' - לזמן פלוני, והקדים לו המעות עכשיו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 63b:10:4.english: I will give you five, five - [Meaning, at a rate of five loaves per dinar] at a specified time, and [the buyer] advanced him the money now.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 63b:10:5.hebrew: איתנהו - אם בידו, אבל אינם בעיר או אבד המפתח והוא דחוק למעות — שרי, דהוי ליה "הלויני עד שיבא בני", דתנן במתניתין (דף עה.) דמותר:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 63b:10:5.english: [If] he has [them] - If [they are] in his possession, but they are not in the city or the key was lost, and he is pressed for money, [it is] permitted, for it is [like the case of] "Lend me until my son comes," which we learned in the Mishnah (75a) is permitted.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 63b:11:1.english: Where he has credit in the town - This seller, too, gave money and contracted with others for wax.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 63b:12:1.english: And he found an excess - The one who received the coins found in them more than what his fellow told him.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 63b:12:2.hebrew: אי בכדי שהדעת טועה - דאיכא למימר טעה המלוה בחשבון ולא ידע בהן, חייב זה להחזירו לו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 63b:12:2.english: If [it is] within [an amount] that the mind errs - Since it can be said [that] the lender erred in the calculation and was unaware of them, this one [the borrower] is obligated to return it to him.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 63b:1:1.hebrew: מה לי דמיהן מה לי הן נמי אמרינן כו' - בתחלת התנאי נמי, שיצא השער, פוסק עמו ואע"פ שאין פירות בידו, ובלבד שיתן לו זה מעות. דכי היכי דאם היו דמי המעות הללו בידו, והיינו הפירות, הוי מותר, הכי נמי כי הוו המעות בידו מותר, שהמעות ודמיהן שוין; דמה לי טוב אם היו החטין, שהם דמים למעות הללו, בידו מעכשיו, שהם עצמן בידו? אף הוא יכול ליקח בהן פירות. ומן הטעם הזה פוסקין על סמך שער שבשוק, והוא שער היוצא על ידי חמרין המביאין תבואה לשוק בכרכים, ואע"פ שאין פירות לזה. וא"ת: משנתינו היא זו (לקמן בבא מציעא דף עב:) "יצא השער פוסקין"! איכא למ"ד לקמן אין פוסקין על שער שבשוק, ומוקי למתניתין באכלבאי וארבי, דמתניתין לאו שער שבשוק תנן, אלא "יצא השער" סתמא. הא דמפיך לישנא ונקט למימר "מה לי דמיהן מה לי הן", משום דבשעת פרעון הוו המעות שמשלם לו דמי הפירות, ושייך למימר "מה טוב הן מדמיהן, כי היכי דהן שרו דמיהן נמי שרו". ובשעת הפיסוק נותן לו זה מעות לקבל חטין בדמי המעות, ומיקרו הפירות דמיהן של מעות, ושייך למימר "מה טוב דמיהן של מעות מהן, כי היכי דדמיהן שרו, אם היו הפירות בידו, הן נמי, כי הוו הן בידו, שרי". קצרו של דבר: לשון הפסקה נמשך אצל לוקח, לשון הפרעון נמשך אחר המוכר. גבי תנאי ראשון פוסק ונותן לו דמים לקבל כנגדן חטין, הלכך החטין קרוין דמים אצל לוקח, דמי מעותיו; וגבי פרעון, המעות שזה פורע הוו דמי החטין שזה חייב לו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 63b:1:1.english: What [difference is it] to me [regarding] their value, what [difference is it] to me [regarding] them themselves, we also say, etc. - At the beginning of the stipulation as well, once the market rate has been established, one may set [a price] with him even though he does not have produce in his possession, provided that this one [the buyer] gives him money. For just as if the value of these coins were in his possession — and that is the produce — it would be permitted, so too when the coins are in his possession it is permitted, since the coins and their value are equal; for what is better to me if the wheat, which is the value for these coins, were in his possession from now, than that they [the coins] themselves are in his possession? He too can purchase produce with them. And for this reason, one may set a price relying on the market rate — which is the rate established by the donkey-drivers who bring grain to the market in the cities — even though this one [the seller] has no produce. And if you will say: This is our Mishnah (below, Bava Metzia 72b), "Once the market rate has been established, one may set a price"! There is an opinion below that one may not set a price based on the market rate, and he establishes our Mishnah as referring to wholesalers and boatmen, for our Mishnah does not teach "the market rate," but rather "the rate has been established" unqualified. This that he reverses the phrasing and adopts the expression "what [difference is it] to me [regarding] their value, what [difference is it] to me [regarding] them themselves" is because at the time of payment, the coins that he pays him are the value of the produce, and [thus] it is appropriate to say, "what is better [about] them [the produce] than their value [the coins]? Just as they are permitted, their value is also permitted." Whereas at the time of setting the price, this one [the buyer] gives him coins to receive wheat for the value of the coins, so the produce is called "the value of the coins," and [thus] it is appropriate to say, "what is better [about] the value of the coins than them [the coins] themselves? Just as their value is permitted — if the produce were in his possession — they themselves also, when they themselves are in his possession, are permitted." The short of the matter: the wording of setting the price follows the buyer, [while] the wording of payment follows the seller. Regarding the first stipulation, he sets a price and gives him money to receive wheat in exchange for it; therefore, the wheat is called "value" with respect to the buyer, the value of his coins; and regarding payment, the coins that this one pays are the value of the wheat that this one owes him.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 63b:2:1.english: [If] he does not have [it], [it is] prohibited - In that [baraita] of Rabbi Oshaya.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 63b:3:1.hebrew: היני ושילי - מקומות הן שהיו סמוכין לפומבדיתא שהיו רבה ורב יוסף יושבין בה; כלומר, בכל מקום הוא מוצא סביבותיו בדמים הללו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 63b:3:1.english: Hini and Shili - They are places that were near Pumbedita, where Rabbah and Rav Yosef resided; that is to say, anywhere in his vicinity he can find [it] at this price.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 63b:4:1.hebrew: חטי דקדחי באכלבאי - בתמיה: וכי אם הנחתי חטים שלי באוצרי, כלום היו גשמים יורדים עליהן שיהיו צומחות בהן צמחים להתקלקל? לישנא אחרינא: דקדחי — לשון חמימות, כמו (ישעיהו סד) כקדח אש:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 63b:4:1.english: Wheat that sprouts [dekadḥei] in my warehouse - [This is said] as a rhetorical question: If I had left my wheat in my storehouse, would rain have fallen upon it so that sprouts would grow in it to spoil? Another explanation: dekadḥei [is] an expression of heat, as [in] (Isaiah 64[:1]): "like the kindling of fire."

Rashi on Bava Metzia 63b:5:1.hebrew: והא בעי למיתב זוזי לספסירא - היכי אמרינן מאי אהני לפסוק על שער שבשוק? והא אהני, דבעי למיתב זוזי לספסירא — סרסור שמבקש למוכרי חטין — נמצא משתכר זוזי בהקדמת המעות:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 63b:5:1.english: But he has to give coins to a broker - How can we say "what benefit is there" to set [a price] at the market rate? Indeed there is a benefit, for [otherwise] he would have to give coins to a broker — an agent who seeks out sellers of wheat — [and thus] he ends up gaining coins by advancing the money.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 63b:5:2.english: And he answers that he gives - The buyer must give the seller the broker's fee.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 63b:5:3.hebrew: רב אשי אמר - לא צריך. זוזי דאיניש עבדי ליה ספסירות — החמרין הולכין אצל בעלי המעות להוליך לו תבואה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 63b:5:3.english: Rav Ashi said - [It is] not necessary [to give the broker's fee]. A person's money performs the brokerage for him — the donkey-drivers go to the owners of the money to bring him grain.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 63b:6:1.hebrew: האי מאן דיהיב זוזי אתרעא חריפא - הפוסק על הפירות עד שלא יצא השער הברור, אלא שער הבכיר, שהיא סמוך לקציר, שהלקוטות מוכרין בזולא, זה סאה וזה סאתים. ותנן מתני' (דף עב:) דאם יש לו, מותר לפסוק ואע"פ שלא יצא השער, דקתני: היה הוא תחילה לקוצרים, פוסק עמו על הגדיש:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 63b:6:1.english: One who gives money at the advance price - [This refers to] one who contracts for produce before the established market price has been published, rather [at] the early price, which is near the harvest, when the gleaners sell cheaply — this one [selling] a se'ah and that one two se'ahs. And we learned in the Mishnah (72b) that if [the seller] has [the produce], it is permitted to contract [with him] even though the market price has not been published, as it teaches: [If] he was the first of the harvesters, one may contract with him for the stack [of grain].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 63b:6:2.hebrew: צריך הלוקח לאיתחזויי אבי דרי - של מוכר כשהוא דש וזורה תבואתו בגורן. ולהכי נקיט תרעא חריפא, שאין פוסקין עליו אלא למי שיש לו גורן, דאילו שער הברור פוסקים אף למי שאין לו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 63b:6:2.english: The buyer must present himself at the granary - [that] of the seller when he is threshing and winnowing his grain on the threshing floor. And this is why [the Gemara] mentions the early price: because one may only fix a price on it for someone who has a granary, whereas [at] the established price, one may fix a price even for someone who does not have [one].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 63b:7:1.english: For what - is this [requirement] that he present himself needed?

Rashi on Bava Metzia 63b:7:2.hebrew: אי למיקני - ממש, שלא יוכל המוכר לחזור:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 63b:7:2.english: If [it is] to acquire - Actually [acquire], so that the seller cannot retract.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 63b:7:3.hebrew: הא לא קני - בהכי, אלא א"כ משך:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 63b:7:3.english: He does not acquire - By this, unless he pulls [the produce].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 63b:7:4.english: If [it is] for the seller to accept upon himself "He Who exacted payment" - If he reneges.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 63b:8:1.hebrew: סמכא דעתא - דכל חד וחד וידע דעליה קא סמיך האי לוקח, וסחורה מקויימת היא, ואין דעתו לחזור. הלכך, אם חזר בו מוכר, איכא למילטייה במי שפרע:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 63b:8:1.english: The mind relies - [The mind] of each and every [seller], and he knows that this buyer is relying upon him, and the transaction is confirmed, and he has no intention of retracting. Therefore, if the seller retracts, there is [grounds] to curse him with "He Who exacted payment."

Rashi on Bava Metzia 63b:9:1.english: Now that you have said - That [the condition] "if he presents himself" is [for the seller's] relying [upon him].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 63b:9:2.hebrew: אפילו - לא מיתחזי אבי דרי נמי, אלא אשכחיה בשוקא לאחר זמן ואמר ליה "חזי דעלך סמכינא", איכא מי שפרע:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 63b:9:2.english: Even - [if] he is not seen at the threshing floor either, rather [the seller] found him in the marketplace after some time and said to him, "See, I am relying upon you," there is [the curse of] mi shepara ("He Who exacted punishment").

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 63b:10:1.hebrew: ואמר ליה יהיבנא לך חמשה בזוזא - פי': לזמן פלוני; איתנהו — שרי, ליתנהו — אסור. אבל ד' בזוזא שרי לפסוק, כיון שכן השער, דפוסקין על שער שבשוק. וא"ת: אמאי אסור לפסוק חמשה בזוזא, מאי שנא מטרשא, דרב נחמן גופיה אמר לקמן (בבא מציעא דף סה.) טרשא שרי, למכור סחורה בהמתנה ביותר מדמיה, ובלבד שלא יפרש [לו] "אם מעכשיו — בפחות"? וי"ל: כיון דאזלי הכא ד' בזוזא, הוי כאילו פירש "אם מעכשיו — בפחות, ואם לזמן פלוני — ביותר". ולפי זה לא שרי ר"נ לקמן טרשא אלא בדבר שאין שומתו ידוע, כגון פרה או טלית, אבל פירות, אם יצא השער — אסור לעשות מהן טרשא:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 63b:10:1.english: And he said to him: I will give you five for a zuz - [This] means: by a specified [future] time; if he has them [in his possession], it is permitted; if he does not have them, it is forbidden. However, it is permitted to contract for four [loaves] for a zuz, since that is the [current] market price, as one may contract [for future delivery] at the market price. And if you ask: Why is it forbidden to contract for five for a zuz — how is this different from tarsha [a credit sale at an elevated price], regarding which Rav Naḥman himself says later (Bava Metzia 65a) that tarsha is permitted, [namely] to sell merchandise on credit for more than its [cash] value, provided that he does not explicitly state [to him], "If [paid] now, for less"? And one can answer: Since here they go at four for a zuz, it is as though he explicitly stated, "If [paid] now, for less, and if for a specified [future] time, for more." And according to this, Rav Naḥman only permits tarsha later in the case of something whose valuation is not known [i.e., has no fixed market price], such as a cow or a cloak; but [as for] produce, once the market price has been established, it is forbidden to transact tarsha with them:

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 63b:11:1.hebrew: מהו דתימא כעד שיבא בני דמי קמ"ל - וא"ת: והא רב נחמן פסק לקמן בשילהי פירקין (בבא מציעא דף עה.) כהלל, דאסר "עד שיבא בני"? וי"ל: דודאי דרך הלואה אסור אפילו סאה בסאה, אבל דרך מקח וממכר כי הכא שרי אפי' ה' בארבע; דאי לאו הכי תקשה, דאפילו רבנן לקמן לא שרו אלא סאה בסאה, אבל סאה בסאתים לא. אלא כדפרישית, דדרך מקח וממכר שרי טפי חמש בארבע מדרך הלואה אפילו סאה בסאה, דהכי שרי לכ"ע. וא"ת: דטפי ה"ל לאתויי הכא דפוסק על הגדיש, דדמיא טפי דהוי מקח וממכר? וי"ל: דפוסק עמו על הגדיש לא שרינן אלא לפסוק עמו בשער לקוטות, אבל לפסוק שוי שיתא בחמשא לא — כיון דאכתי לית ליה, שעדיין צריך תיקון, ואי מוזיל גביה כולי האי מחזי כאגר נטר. אבל כשיש לו מזומן בעין, אלא שמחוסר ביאת בנו או הבאת מפתח, מותר אפילו שוי חמשא בארבע. וה"ק: נעשה כ"עד שיבא בני", ושרי הכא לכ"ע כדשרי התם לרבנן:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 63b:11:1.english: "Lest you say it is like 'until my son comes,' [therefore] he teaches us" - And if you ask: Did not Rav Nachman rule later at the end of our chapter (Bava Metzia 75a) in accordance with Hillel, who forbids [the case of] "until my son comes"? One can answer: Certainly by way of a loan it is forbidden, even a se'ah for a se'ah, but by way of buying and selling, such as here, it is permitted even five [worth of goods] for four. For if not so, it would be difficult, since even the Rabbis later only permit a se'ah for a se'ah, whereas a se'ah for two se'ah [they do] not [permit]. Rather, [it must be] as I have explained: that by way of buying and selling, five for four is more permitted than even a se'ah for a se'ah by way of a loan, for in this manner it is permitted according to everyone. And if you ask: It would have been more fitting to bring here [the case of] one who contracts for a stack [of grain], which is more similar since it is [a case of] buying and selling? One can answer: When one contracts with him for a stack [of grain], we only permit contracting with him at the market rate of the gleaners, whereas contracting [for goods] worth six for five is not [permitted], since he does not yet have it [ready], as it still requires processing, and if he reduces the price for him by so much, it appears like a reward for waiting. However, when he has it ready at hand, and it is only lacking his son's arrival or the bringing of the key, it is permitted even [for goods] worth five for four. And this is what [the Gemara] is saying: it is rendered like "until my son comes," and it is permitted here according to everyone, just as it is permitted there according to the Rabbis.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 63b:1:1.hebrew: ופוסקין על שער שבשוק אע"פ שאין לו - פ"ה: "וא"ת מתני' היא: 'יצא השער, פוסקין'? איכא למ"ד אין פוסקין על שער שבשוק, ומוקי לה למתני' באכלבאי וארבי." ולא היה לו לפרש כן, דאפילו לר' יוחנן דאמר לקמן "אין פוסקין על שער שבשוק", מודה דלא בעינן תרעא דמשיך כולי האי כמו אכלבאי וארבי, ולא בעי אלא כדורמוס, ולא אמר ר' יוחנן דאין פוסקין אלא בשוק של עיירות. וא"ת: והיכי שמעינן מר' ינאי דפוסק על שוק של עיירות ולא בעינן דורמוס? וי"ל: דהכי דייק מדאמר רבי ינאי "מה לי הן, מה לי דמיהן" — ויכול לפרוע לו דמים כמו שיכול לפרוע לו חטין, משום דמן החטין יכול למצוא דמים — ה"נ פוסקין אפילו על שוק של עיירות, דיותר יזדמן לבעל המעות לקנות חטין אפי' בשוק של עיירות ממה שיזדמן לבעל חטין למכור אפילו בשוק של אכלבאי וארבי:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 63b:1:1.english: And one may set [a price] by the market rate even though he does not have [it] - The Kuntres [Rashi] explained: "And if you will say, is this not [already] a Mishnah: 'Once the [market] rate has been publicized, one may set [a price]'? There is an authority who says that one may not set [a price] by the market rate, and he establishes the Mishnah [as speaking] of [wheat from] warehouses and ships." But he should not have explained it this way, for even according to Rabbi Yoḥanan, who says later [on 72b], "One may not set [a price] by the market rate," he concedes that we do not require a rate that lasts so long like [that of] warehouses and ships, and he only requires [a market] like a central market [dormus]; and Rabbi Yoḥanan only said that one may not set [a price] in the market of [small] towns. And if you will ask: How do we learn from Rabbi Yannai that one may set [a price] by the market of [small] towns and that we do not require a central market [dormus]? One can answer: He infers this from what Rabbi Yannai said, "What difference is it to me [if it is] the produce itself, [and] what difference is it to me [if it is] its value" — [meaning] he can pay him money just as he can pay him wheat, because from the wheat one can obtain money — so too, one may set [a price] even by the market of [small] towns, for it is more readily available for the owner of the money to buy wheat even in the market of [small] towns than it is for the owner of wheat to sell [it] even in the market of warehouses and ships.
